summary: CMS feature testing complete. Backend: 37/37 pytest tests PASSED (28 prior + 9 new for SiteContent: GET /api/content public, PUT /api/admin/content auth-gated + round-trip persistence, POST /api/admin/upload auth-gated + valid PNG/JPEG accepted + non-image rejected with 400 + >4MB rejected with 400). Frontend: admin login -> /admin shows 3 tabs (Encomendas, Produtos, Conteúdo do site). Clicking the new admin-tab-content renders ContentEditor with all 6 sections (Hero, A Quintinha, Contactos, Avaliações, Categorias, Outros). Editing hero subtitle and clicking Guardar alterações triggers PUT /api/admin/content (200), shows 'Conteúdo guardado' toast, and persists — verified by GET /api/content + by Homepage rendering the new value via ContentProvider. Contact page shows phone/email/address from API content. ImagePicker 'Carregar ficheiro' button visible. Existing flows (orders, products, push banner) still intact.
critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/admin/upload reads full body before checking size — a malicious admin could send arbitrary bytes that get fully buffered in memory before the 4 MB check fails. Consider streaming/early-rejecting via Content-Length header (request.headers.get('content-length')) to avoid OOM on huge payloads. Low risk because endpoint is admin-auth-gated.

Storing base64 data: URLs inside the SiteContent JSON document means a few large images can push the doc near MongoDB's 16 MB BSON limit. With 4 MB raw -> ~5.5 MB base64 per image, hero+about+4 categories could approach the cap. Consider GridFS or external storage (S3/local fs + URL) for production. Fine for MVP.

ContentEditor saves the entire SiteContent payload on every Guardar — last-write-wins. No optimistic concurrency / etag. If two admins edit simultaneously one will silently overwrite the other. Acceptable for single-admin shop.
GET /api/content has no cache headers — every page load re-fetches. Consider Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 with revalidation, or move to a memoized in-process cache invalidated on PUT.

ImagePicker accepts URL paste field — no validation that the URL is actually an image or reachable. A typo would render a broken image on the public site. Suggest a small client-side check (img onload/onerror) before saving.

ContentEditor uses local 'draft' state seeded from useContent(); if context updates after mount (slow fetch) the draft may not refresh. Verified manually — initial render after refetch looks correct because draft is initialised from the latest context, but a useEffect to sync draft when content prop changes would be safer.
SiteContent model lacks length limits on free-text fields (e.g., subtitle, paragraph1). An admin could paste megabytes of text and bloat the doc. Add max_length validation.

/api/admin/content does not return 422 for completely missing payload because all sub-models have defaults — this is intentional (partial updates work) but should be documented; otherwise admins might think a no-op PUT did nothing.
seed_data_creation: Round-trip test temporarily mutates hero.subtitle and contact.phone, then restores. Frontend test mutates hero.subtitle then restores to the original Portuguese copy. No leftover TEST_ data in site_content collection.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CMS endpoints (/api/content, /api/admin/content, /api/admin/upload) have 9 dedicated pytest cases in TestSiteContent. Test helper _make_png_bytes() generates a valid 4x4 red PNG (~70 bytes) to avoid relying on external image libs. JPEG test uses a hand-crafted 1x1 minimal JPEG. Upload size test uses a 5 MB zero buffer claimed as image/png — backend correctly rejects via len(contents) > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES check. Frontend Playwright e2e verified: PUT request fires, 200 response, 'Conteúdo guardado' toast renders, GET reflects new value, Homepage subtitle updates via ContentProvider. /contactos reads phone/email/address from API. ImagePicker present in About section with 'Carregar ficheiro' button. All 37 pytest cases pass in 5.76s. Existing 28 tests untouched.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. CMS round-trip (GET → edit → PUT → GET → render in pages) works end-to-end. Auth gating, file-type validation, and size validation all correctly enforced on backend. Admin tab + ContentEditor + 6 sections + Save-with-toast + dynamic page rendering all verified on frontend.
